metadata.title: Local conditions for exponentially many subdivisions

extraction_notes.note: The three parts of Theorem 2 are proved in separate prose blocks and Theorem 6's proof relies on parts (i) and (ii), so each part is a claim nested in TP6; their statements start after the \item[(i)] tokens.

The proof of Theorem 2 is written in running prose split by Lemma 4 and Claim 5; the transition sentence 'We now turn to the proof of (ii), which will follow from the next lemma.' is left out of every node.
open_problem or remark: the concluding section suggests restating Tuza's question with another local condition, phrased as 'it would be of interest' rather than a precise question.
Cited results stated in a single prose sentence each (Jung's construction, Tuza's bounds); emitted as external theorems rather than left inside the introduction text.

The first paragraph of the concluding remarks restates Theorem 2 and the Theorem 2(ii) construction, so it gets no node; the Bollobás–Thomason / Komlós–Szemerédi verification sentence is not stated in full and gets no node.

nodes.name: Proof.
nodes.statement: Let x_1,ldots,x_k be the branch vertices of K_k in T. Now T is the union of a set lbrace P(i,j): ij in binom[k]2 rbrace of internally vertex-disjoint paths where P(i,j) has endpoints x_i, x_j. Then we can find a copy of TK_ell with branch vertices x_1,ldots,x_ell by taking the paths P(i,j) for all lbrace i,j rbrace in binom[ell]2 setminus lbrace 1,ell rbrace, and taking the concatenation of the paths P(ell,ell+1), P(ell+1,ell+2), ldots, P(k-1,k),P(1,k) to obtain a path between x_1 and x_ell which contains every other branch vertex in V(T).

Let $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ be the branch vertices of $K_k$ in $T$.
Now $T$ is the union of a set $\lbrace P(i,j): ij \in \binom{[k]}{2} \rbrace$ of internally vertex-disjoint paths where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i, x_j$.
Then we can find a copy of $TK_\ell$ with branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ by taking the paths $P(i,j)$ for all $\lbrace i,j \rbrace \in \binom{[\ell]}{2} \setminus \lbrace  1,\ell \rbrace$, and taking the concatenation of the paths $P(\ell,\ell+1), P(\ell+1,\ell+2), \ldots, P(k-1,k),P(1,k)$
to obtain a path between $x_1$ and $x_\ell$ which contains every other branch vertex in $V(T)$.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

nodes.statement: Let G be a graph with vertex partition A cup B, where B is an independent set. Let F be a graph on ell geq |A| vertices. Then s(F,G) leq 2^ell (|B|+1)^e(F)+2ell.
assumptions: Let G be a graph with vertex partition A cup B, where B is an independent set.
Let F be a graph on ell geq |A| vertices.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{semibip}
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex partition $A \cup B$, where $B$ is an independent set.
Let $F$ be a graph on $\ell \geq |A|$ vertices.
Then $s(F,G) \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}$.
nodes.clean_text: Let G be a graph with vertex partition A cup B, where B is an independent set. Let F be a graph on ell geq |A| vertices. Then s(F,G) leq 2^ell (|B|+1)^e(F)+2ell.
nodes.label: semibip

nodes.name: Proof.
nodes.statement: Write V(F) = [ell]. Let T be a subdivision of F in G, and let x_1,ldots,x_ell be its branch vertices. So T consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths P(i,j) for all ij in E(F), where P(i,j) has endpoints x_i,x_j. Denote by P the union of the P(i,j). Let P(A,A) be the set of P(i,j) such that x_i,x_j in A, and define P(A,B) = P(B,A) and P(B,B) analogously. Given P = P(i,j), let a_P be the number of internal vertices of P which lie in A, i.e.~a_P := |A cap (V(P)setminus lbrace x_i,x_j rbrace)| and define b_P analogously for B. Since B is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see: b_P &leq a_P+1 for all P in P(A,A);\\ b_P &leq a_P for all P in P(A,B);\\ b_P &leq a_P-1 for all P in P(B,B). Then, since |P|= e(F), ell geq |A| geq sum_P in Pa_P geq sum_P in P(b_P-1)=sum_P in Pb_P-|P| Rightarrow sum_P in Pb_P le ell+|P|= ell+e(F). Denote by b^* the number of branch vertices of T which lie in B. Clearly, b^*le ell, hence, |V(T) cap B| = b^* + sum_P in Pb_P leq 2ell + e(F). Therefore an upper bound for s(F,G) can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of V(G) containing at most 2ell+e(F) vertices in B. Thus s(F,G) leq 2^|A| cdot sum_i = 0^2ell + e(F) binom|B|i leq 2^ell (|B|+1)^e(F)+2ell, proving the lemma.
nodes.raw_latex:
Write $V(F) = [\ell]$.
Let $T$ be a subdivision of $F$ in $G$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ be its branch vertices.
So $T$ consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(F)$, where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i,x_j$.
Denote by $\mathcal{P}$ the union of the $P(i,j)$.
Let $\mathcal{P}(A,A)$ be the set of $P(i,j)$ such that $x_i,x_j \in A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(A,B) = \mathcal{P}(B,A)$ and $\mathcal{P}(B,B)$ analogously.
Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j \rbrace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$.
Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see:
\begin{align*}
b_P &\leq a_P+1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\\
b_P &\leq a_P \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\\
b_P &\leq a_P-1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B).
\end{align*}
Then, since $|\mathcal{P}|= e(F)$,
\begin{align*}
\ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\mathcal{P}|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\mathcal{P}|= \ell+e(F).
\end{align*}
Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, 
$$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$

Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$.
Thus
$$
s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)} \binom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell},
$$
proving the lemma.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

nodes.statement: Let J be the set of copies of K_ell-1 containing e and let K be the set of copies of K_ell^- containing e. So |J| = g(e) and |K| geq t. Now, every copy of K_ell^- containing e contains exactly two distinct J in J as subgraphs. So, by averaging, there is some J in J such that there is K' subseteq K with the property that J subseteq K for all K in K' and |K'| geq frac2|K|g(e)ge 2t^1-varepsilon. Every K in K' has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in V(J). Averaging once again we see that there is some z in V(J) and K'' subseteq K' such that for all K in K'' every y in V(K) is incident with every x in V(J) setminus lbrace z rbrace; and |K''| geq frac|K'|ell-1 stackrel()geq frac2t^1-varepsilonell-1. Now, let A := V(J) and let B := bigcup_K in K''V(K) setminus V(J). Every K in K'' contains precisely one vertex x_K outside of V(J) and the only non-adjacent pair in K is x_Kz. Therefore the vertices x_K are distinct for distinct K. So |B| = |K''|, as required. The remaining properties are clear. It will suffice to give a lower bound for s(K_ell^-,H). We will count the number of subdivisions T of K_ell^- in H with specific properties. Label the vertices of K_ell^- by 1,ldots,ell, where E(K_ell^-) = binom[ell]2setminus lbrace ell-1,ell rbrace. Write A = lbrace x_1,ldots,x_ell-1 := z rbrace. Let x_ell and x_ij for all ij in binom[ell-2]2 be arbitrary distinct vertices in B and let X be the set consisting of these vertices. Using these we can find a subdivision T(X) of K_ell^- in H with vertex set A cup X, branch vertices x_1,ldots,x_ell and paths P(i,j) for all ij in E(K_ell^-), as follows. item For all i in [ell-1], the vertex x_i in A corresponds to i in V(K_ell^-), and the vertex x_ell in B corresponds to ell in V(K_ell^-). item For all ij in binom[ell-2]2, each P(i,j) has precisely one internal vertex x_ij, which lies in B. For all i in [ell-2] and j in lbrace ell-1,ell rbrace, P(i,j) is the edge x_ix_j. Note that T(X) exists because H[A] is complete and H[A setminus lbrace x_ell-1 rbrace,B] is complete bipartite. Different choices of X give rise to distinguishable T(X) since V(T(X)) = A cup X. Each X has order binomell-22+1, so s(K_ell^-,G) &geq& s(K_ell^-,H) geq binom|B|binomell-22+1 geq left(frac2t^1-varepsilon(ell-1)left(binomell-22+1right)right)^binomell-22+1\\ & geq &t^(1-2varepsilon)left(binomell-22+1right)= t^(1-2varepsilon)(e(K_ell^-)-2ell+5), completing the proof of (iii). This concludes the proof of Theorem~. square
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$.
So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$.
Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs.
So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and
\begin{equation}\label{K}
|\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}.
\end{equation}
Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$.
Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and
$$
|\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{\ell-1}.
$$
Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$.
Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$.
Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$.
So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required.
The remaining properties are clear.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

\medskip
\noindent
It will suffice to give a lower bound for $s(K_\ell^-,H)$.
We will count the number of subdivisions $T$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with specific properties.
Label the vertices of $K_\ell^-$ by $1,\ldots,\ell$, where $E(K_\ell^-) = \binom{[\ell]}{2}\setminus \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$.
Write $A = \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_{\ell-1} := z \rbrace$.
Let $x_\ell$ and $x_{ij}$ for all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$ be arbitrary distinct vertices in $B$ and let $X$ be the set consisting of these vertices.
Using these we can find a subdivision $T(X)$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with vertex set $A \cup X$, branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ and paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(K_\ell^-)$, as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item For all $i \in [\ell-1]$, the vertex $x_i \in A$ corresponds to $i \in V(K_\ell^-)$, and the vertex $x_\ell \in B$ corresponds to $\ell \in V(K_\ell^-)$.
\item For all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$, each $P(i,j)$ has precisely one internal vertex $x_{ij}$, which lies in $B$. For all $i \in [\ell-2]$ and $j \in \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$, $P(i,j)$ is the edge $x_ix_j$. 
\end{itemize}
Note that $T(X)$ exists because $H[A]$ is complete and $H[A \setminus \lbrace x_{\ell-1} \rbrace,B]$ is complete bipartite. Different choices of $X$ give rise to distinguishable $T(X)$ since $V(T(X)) = A \cup X$.
Each $X$ has order $\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1$, so
\begin{eqnarray*}
s(K_\ell^-,G) &\geq& s(K_\ell^-,H) \geq \binom{|B|}{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1} \geq \left(\frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{(\ell-1)\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}\right)^{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1}\\
& \geq &t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}= t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)},
\end{eqnarray*}
completing the proof of (iii).
This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}.
\hfill$\square$

nodes.statement: We say that a graph G is (F,k,t)-locally dense if every edge of G lies in at least t copies of F' for all subgraphs F' subseteq F with |F'| geq k.
nodes.raw_latex: We say that a graph $G$ is \emph{$(F,k,t)$-locally dense} if every edge of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F'$ for all subgraphs $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$.

nodes.statement: For (i), let F be a graph on ell vertices containing a copy of K_k. Let G be a (F,k,t)-locally dense graph. Then G is certainly (K_k,t)-locally dense. The conclusion follows immediately from Theorem~(i). For (ii), note that F is K_k-free if and only if every subgraph F' subseteq F with |F'| geq k is such that F' contains a pair of non-adjacent vertices. Therefore the graph G we constructed in the proof of Theorem~(ii) is in fact (F,k,t)-dense. (To see this, one can use the same argument, as there is always a non-adjacent pair in F' which can we embed into B in at least t different ways.) The conclusion follows from Lemma~.
nodes.raw_latex:
For (i), let $F$ be a graph on $\ell$ vertices containing a copy of $K_k$.
Let $G$ be a $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graph.
Then $G$ is certainly $(K_k,t)$-locally dense.
The conclusion follows immediately from Theorem~\ref{main}(i).

For (ii), note that $F$ is $K_k$-free if and only if every subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$ is such that $F'$ contains a pair of non-adjacent vertices.
Therefore the graph $G$ we constructed in the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}(ii) is in fact $(F,k,t)$-dense.
(To see this, one can use the same argument, as there is always a non-adjacent pair in $F'$ which can we embed into $B$ in at least $t$ different ways.) The conclusion follows from Lemma~\ref{semibip}.
